analysis.title: "Spend Now, Monetize Later": Wall Street Cheers SpaceX's Blowout As 2027 Capex Estimates Approach $300 Billion
key_insights: SpaceX Q3 results beat: revenue of $14.6B (+161% YoY) vs consensus $12.9B, adjusted EBITDA of $8.8B (+306%) vs Street $6.6B. SPCX rose almost 10% to $162 in early trading and every covering bank raised numbers, most raised targets.

Super Intelligence (formerly AI) segment revenue was $7.6B, up 830% YoY and 195% QoQ, now larger than Starlink and just over half of total revenue. Per Goldman's Sean Johnstone, about 93% of SI revenue came from compute sales and leasing, Cursor added $608M and advertising $0.5B.

Guidance: Q1 2027 revenue of $33-37B vs consensus of about $23B. About 13GW of compute by end-2027 (up from 5-10GW prior), 1.7GW nameplate in Q3, 2.5-3GW targeted by year-end. Incremental compute pricing above $50 per watt vs prior $30-50, and a $63B backlog.

Musk now targets $500B to $1T of annual recurring revenue by end-2027, versus $1T as a 2030 target in August. Wolfe's Myles Walton calculates this at about $50B of ARR per GW on 13GW. Mizuho's Brett Linzey treats the ARR target as aspirational.

Quality-of-beat caveats: $4.4B net income included about $1B of other income and a $390M tax benefit. GAAP SI operating income of $431M missed Goldman and consensus. Starlink added 1.6M subscribers vs 2.2M consensus, launches were 35 vs 41 expected, and compute capacity of 1.7GW was just under the 1.74GW consensus.

2027 revenue estimates jumped: Goldman +51% to $192.5B, Deutsche Bank +45% to $181B, Wolfe +36% to $213B. Mizuho lifted 2027 EBITDA to $100.5B from $64.2B. Wolfe raised 2027 EBITDA by $34B and 2027 free cash flow burn by $73B to $109B.

Price targets: Goldman $245 from $230 (Buy), Citi $240 from $200, Mizuho $205. Street targets sit 26% to 85% above the current price. Wolfe notes the stock trades at 9.4x 2027 sales vs 21x average in the two years before the IPO.

Q4 capex guided to $35-40B, roughly double the $19.6B just spent and above Street (Citi had $27.8B). Goldman models free cash flow burn of $55.5B this year and $172B in 2027 with capex of $292B, $150B of new debt next year, long-term debt rising from $22B (end-2025) to $175B, and cash falling to $7B by end-2028 from about $90B at end of Q3.

Deutsche Bank's Edison Yu models 2027 capex above $285B, back-end loaded, supported by $140B of debt/structured financing, giving credit for 10GW rather than 13GW by end-2027. Citi models $291B of 2027 capex and $305B in 2028, with long-term debt reaching $300B by 2028 and net debt to equity rising from -22% to 76%.

Across Goldman, DB and Citi, about $160-175B of 2027 capex is not covered by EBITDA. JonesTrading's Mike O'Rourke estimates 10GW costs about $500B at Jensen Huang's $50B per GW figure, and suggests Nvidia could offer buy-now-pay-later financing. SpaceX claims about $35B per GW, a third below the industry.

Bond market skepticism: SpaceX sold $25B of BBB-rated bonds shortly after its $86B IPO and bondholders have been underwater since. The 6.65% notes due 2056 hit an all-time low of 83.3 cents on the dollar (yield about 8.1%) before the print and slumped back after a brief bounce. A further $40B Apollo-arranged chip loan was raised this month and five-year CDS hit a record. The sell-side expects $150-265B of new SpaceX debt by 2028 per Goldman and Citi.

Pricing and contract quality: most announced hosting deals run $35-50M annual revenue per MW and are described as 90-day cancellable on both sides. The above-$50/W pricing applies to shorter-term contracts. The article estimates SpaceX AI segment realizes about $18 per watt per year, roughly a third of the quoted short-term rate and in line with AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. Anthropic is the biggest disclosed compute customer and plans to spend up to $750B on compute per the WSJ.

SpaceX and Tesla formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger. Prediction markets price 66% odds of a deal by end-2027. RBC's Tom Narayan says a deal may need a premium of about $480 per TSLA share, implying a roughly 50/50 split even though SpaceX is about 70% of pro forma value. A deal needs a majority of all Tesla shares outstanding.

Near-term flow risk: per Wolfe, 1.3B shares come off lockup Thursday, the largest tranche of the year, similar to the setup before the stock's 14% slide after its first earnings report in August. Goldman's TMT desk (Peter Bartlett) called the print a beat vs consensus but soft vs whisper, and the desk was a net seller of Semis/AI into the bounce.

Read-across: Alphabet -1% and Microsoft -0.5% as SpaceX emerges as a new competitor. JPM's Andrew Tyler said the beat and Super Micro's preannouncement would not resolve investor concerns about financing risk and the scale of AI capex. Meta reports tonight as the first live test of capex discipline under FCF pressure, and per JPM most investors expect Meta to raise equity after Q3.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Eric Sheridan reiterated Buy and raised the target from $230, citing strong operating momentum across all segments and a positive risk/reward skew with shares about 25% below post-IPO peak close. Goldman lists funding needs as an overhang.

Citi's John Godyn raised the target from $200, citing a track record of beats and raises, $/watt trending above consensus, and Starship Flight 15 as a catalyst. Citi calls its targets a heavily discounted version of $900+/share.
Mizuho's Brett Linzey raised the target and treats the $500B-$1T ARR target as aspirational.
Wolfe says it will look to raise its multiple after a successful Starship Flight Test 15, and is not a fan of the Tesla merger but resigned to its inevitability.
Deutsche Bank raised 2027 revenue 45% to $181B, assumes $/GW pricing falls 25% by 2028, and gives credit for 10GW rather than 13GW by end-2027.

sector_views.rationale: Demand exceeds supply and the SpaceX print revived the AI trade, but sell-side models show capex far above EBITDA, requiring heavy debt issuance. JPM's desk remains tactically bullish while flagging financing risk.

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q3 2026 reported 10/20: revenue $14.6B vs consensus $12.9B, adjusted EBITDA $8.8B vs Street $6.6B, net income $4.4B reported including about $1B other income and a $390M tax benefit. GAAP SI operating income $431M reported, missed Goldman and consensus, largely on about $1.2B of Cursor-related acquisition costs and stock compensation.

SpaceX Q3 operational misses vs consensus: Starlink net adds 1.6M vs 2.2M est, ARPU $69 reported, launches 35 vs 41 est, compute capacity 1.7GW vs 1.74GW est. Connectivity margin was flat/weak per Citi.

SpaceX guidance: Q1 2027 revenue $33-37B vs consensus about $23B, Q4 capex $35-40B vs Citi estimate $27.8B, 13GW compute by end-2027, $100B ARR by end of 2026 reiterated in August, $500B-$1T ARR by end-2027.

Meta reports Q3 earnings tonight (10/21), with the market watching whether it holds 2026/27 capex while FCF is under pressure. Tesla reports tonight with the merger question open. Super Micro preannounced strong results.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A high long-end yield raises the cost of the new debt issuance the sell-side expects from SpaceX and other AI borrowers, which compete for the same duration buyers.

risk_factors: Funding overhang: Goldman warns potential future funding needs will weigh on the stock until visibility on capital raises improves.
Capex and FCF: Goldman sees 2027 FCF of -$172B and capex of $292B. A $160-175B gap between 2027 capex and EBITDA must be financed.
Credit market capacity: SpaceX bonds yield about 8.1% on the 2056 notes and the 10Y is at 5.12%. Hyperscalers, neoclouds, Oracle and Meta's Hyperion SPV compete for the same buyers.
Pricing normalization: Deutsche Bank notes investors worry pricing could normalize in 2028-29 and already assumes $/GW pricing falls 25% by 2028. Contracts are short-dated, many 90-day cancellable.
Customer concentration and circularity: biggest disclosed compute customer is Anthropic, which needs to raise up to $750B for compute.
Lockup expiry of 1.3B shares on Thursday.
Tesla merger complexity: a deal needs a majority of all Tesla shares outstanding, which Musk called quite a high hurdle, and may require a large premium.
charts_described: Wolfe's estimate table shows 2027 adjusted EBITDA raised by $34B and 2027 free cash flow burn raised by $73B to $109B.
Chart of SpaceX 6.65% notes due 2056 shows a drop to an all-time low of 83.3 cents on the dollar before the print, a brief rally after, then a return to lifetime lows just above 83 cents.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's TMT desk said Tuesday's move higher felt squeezy with short pockets at the top of the leader board, and the desk was still a net seller of Semis/AI into the bounce.
1.3B SpaceX shares come off lockup on Thursday, the largest tranche of the year, per Wolfe. The stock fell 14% after its first earnings report in August, ahead of a prior unlock.
SpaceX five-year CDS blew out to a record earlier this month. Oracle CDS is at record highs and Paramount CDS is at financial-crisis levels per the author's own tweet on 10/7.
cross_bank_references: Citi's John Godyn says management went out of its way to make clear how far ahead the company was tracking vs. consensus.
Goldman's Johnstone calls the quarter the cleanest AI-segment ramp yet.
Wolfe's Myles Walton points out ARR target works out to about $50B per GW on about 13GW.
DB gives SpaceX credit for 10GW by end-2027, not 13GW, while Goldman, Citi and management use 13GW.
JonesTrading's O'Rourke estimates 10GW at about $500B, in line with Jensen Huang's $50B per GW, versus SpaceX's claim of $35B per GW per DB's estimate.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand exceeds supply, SpaceX says it can build a gigawatt for a third less than peers, and if payback drops to six months the math works on its own. Goldman's Sheridan sees a positive risk/reward skew with shares about 25% below the post-IPO peak.
tension_points.bear_case: 2027 capex of about $290B exceeds EBITDA by $160-175B and must be funded with $150-265B of new debt by 2028, against short-dated contracts, realized pricing near $18/W vs $50/W quoted, and a bond market already pricing SpaceX like high yield.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Visibility on capital raises (Goldman says funding needs will be an overhang until then), pricing normalizing in 2028-29 (DB assumes a 25% drop by 2028), or failure of the new bond issuance to clear.

tension_points.bull_case: Musk says there is a lot of merit for combining the companies. Morgan Stanley's Jonas lays out synergies in compute, connectivity and capital.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC says SpaceX holders would contribute about 70% of value but get under half the company at a roughly $480 per TSLA share premium. A deal needs a majority of all Tesla shares outstanding, and a merged entity would pair SpaceX capex with Tesla's balance sheet.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to reach a majority of all Tesla shares outstanding, which Musk called quite a high hurdle.
